content.title: Deutsche Bank, facing probe, posts biggest annual profit in nearly two decades
content.summary:
STORY: A day after Frankfurt prosecutors raided Germany's largest lender, Deutsche Bank on Thursday posted its largest annual profit since 2007 after a stronger-than-expected fourth quarter.

The bank recorded net profit attributable to shareholders of $7.3 billion for 2025,

helped by strength at its global investment bank.

It was slightly ahead of analyst expectations.

It's sixth consecutive year in the black is welcome after a rocky decade saw big losses and fears among regulators the bank was teetering.

The 2025 financial year also closes out a three-year financial plan.

The bank pledged and met a key profit target - so-called return on tangible equity - of more than 10%.

:: File

The results were overshadowed by prosecutors' searches this week highlighting a recurring issue of money laundering lapses at Deutsche Bank over the last decade.

Frankfurt prosecutors said they were investigating as-yet unidentified individuals and bank employees.

Two insiders told Reuters the case involved transactions between 2013 and 2018.

Deutsche said it was cooperating.
